facts.text: Manhattan Beach was the most upscale of the three major resort areas that developed at Coney Island shortly after the Civil War.
Austin Corbin, former LIRR president, built the Manhattan Beach Hotel in 1877 and the grander Oriental Hotel in 1880, turning the area into a seaside resort.
Sousa composed the “Manhattan Beach” march in 1893 to commemorate the beach resort.
During World War II, the Coast Guard operated a training station at Manhattan Beach, and from 1954 to 1959 the neighborhood housed the Manhattan Beach Air Force Station.
The Manhattan Beach Historical Society, founded as the City Historical Committee in 1970 and incorporated in 1977, preserves the city’s history and operates a museum in Polliwog Park.
After WWII, a large influx of people moved to Manhattan Beach for year‑round living, leading to extensive development east of Sepulveda.
